questions.q: What are ServiceNow's three UI generations, in order?
options: Classic UI (UI11/UI15), UI16, and Workspaces
UI16, Classic UI, and Agent Workspace
Mobile, Desktop, and Tablet
Service Portal, Now Mobile, and UI Builder
questions.explain: The Classic UI came first, UI16 became the modern standard, and Workspaces are the newest generation.

questions.q: What is UI16, in terms of the screens it produces?
options: A mobile-only rendering mode
The navigator-plus-list-plus-form pattern that most non-workspace screens still use
A replacement database engine
A deprecated interface no longer available on any instance
questions.explain: UI16 is the Application Navigator, list views, and forms pattern — still the default for most of the instance.

options: They can't be built — only ServiceNow itself can create them
UI Builder (ServiceNow's low-code screen designer), or shipped out-of-box like Agent Workspace
A separate programming language unrelated to the Now Platform
Third-party design software outside ServiceNow entirely
questions.explain: Workspaces are built with UI Builder, or ServiceNow ships some out-of-box, such as Agent Workspace.

questions.q: What is the real tradeoff between UI16/Classic UI and a workspace?
options: There is no real tradeoff — workspaces are strictly better in every way
UI16 gives access to everything via one consistent pattern; a workspace is faster and more focused for one job but narrower in scope
Workspaces give access to every table on the instance, while UI16 only shows one table
UI16 is only available on mobile devices
questions.explain: UI16's generality covers the whole instance; a workspace trades that breadth for speed and focus on a single job.

questions.q: Why do most ServiceNow instances run both UI16/Classic UI and workspaces at the same time?
options: Workspaces replace UI16 entirely once configured, so this never actually happens
UI16 is required for the instance to load at all, regardless of workspaces
A workspace is narrow in scope, so UI16/Classic UI stays available for administration and anything without a purpose-built workspace
Running both is a temporary migration step with no long-term use
questions.explain: Workspaces cover specific roles and jobs; UI16/Classic UI remains the general-purpose fallback for everything else.
